clue.text: Rough cover left on casing of uranium

parts.note: a hood is a head covering

indicators.note: the casing of a word is its outside, so only its first and last letters are taken

explanation.surface: Instructions for some rough protective cover laid over a uranium casing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough' looks like an adjective but is a noun here: a rough is a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough is a violent ruffian or street thug, the same as a gangland heavy.

clue.text: Social creature runs away with beloved animals

parts.note: the ant lives in highly organised colonies, a classic social insect
to elope is to run off secretly with a lover to marry

explanation.surface: A gregarious creature abandons its herd to run away with its sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: Gazelles, gnus and impalas are examples of these hoofed grazing animals.

clue.text: The old folk, one a Gulf inhabitant

parts.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the
folk means people, men
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: The elderly people, one of them living by the Gulf.
explanation.definitionFit: Yemen borders the Gulf of Aden, so a native of that country lives on the Gulf.

clue.text: Angry about university recruitment, essentially, following good financial gift

indicators.note: following says the rest comes after the letter for good
about says the word for angry wraps around the other letters

parts.note: ratty is informal for irritable or angry

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its central letter, here the middle one of recruitment

explanation.surface: Someone is furious that a university's hiring followed a generous gift of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' gives I, the middle letter of 'recruitment', which joins U inside RATTY.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip is money freely given in thanks for service, a small financial present.

clue.text: Rile person by acquiring their browser?

definitions.meaning: an idiom meaning to annoy or irritate somebody
read literally, obtaining somebody's grazing animal, since a goat browses on shrubs

explanation.surface: Annoying someone by getting hold of their web browser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'browser' suggests internet software, but here it is an animal that browses on leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to irritate somebody intensely; literally it would mean taking their goat.

clue.text: Supplies of aid from harassed prison-guard lacking working gun

indicators.note: harassed means flustered and in disarray, so the letters of prison-guard are jumbled
lacking says the letters of the gun, itself treated as working fodder, are struck out of the mixed pool

parts.note: anagram fodder taken as written
letters taken as written and removed from the fodder

explanation.surface: A harassed prison guard, deprived of a working gun, seeks help.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of PRISON-GUARD equal the answer plus GUN, so take G, U, N out and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Parachuted deliveries from aircraft are a common way of getting relief supplies to people.

clue.text: Worry mates publicly climbing houses

indicators.note: climbing says the hidden letters are read backwards
houses says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Friends worrying about publicly scaling houses.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'climbing' means read upwards, so TESPU, hidden in 'mates publicly', is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: To worry someone is to distress or trouble them, the same as to upset them.

clue.text: Frenzy almost following reduction of time for orchestral instruments

indicators.note: following says the frenzy word comes after the shortened time
a reduction of the word time leaves it short of its final letter
almost means the word for frenzy loses its last letter

parts.note: panic is a state of frantic alarm

explanation.surface: Near-hysteria follows a cut in rehearsal time for the orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Kettledrums are the tuned percussion in a symphony orchestra's back row.

clue.text: Vitality of black feline

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the ounce is another name for the snow leopard

explanation.surface: The liveliness of a black cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Bounce in this sense is energy, zest and lively spirit.

clue.text: Irritating, varying rise in volume

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the word for volume

parts.note: a tome is a large book or volume

indicators.note: varying means changing, so the letters of rise are rearranged

explanation.surface: An annoying fluctuating rise in loudness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volume' suggests loudness, but here it is a book; 'varying' signals the rearranged letters, and 'in' places them within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wearisome and annoying is tedious and grating, as a bore is.

clue.text: Organised isle ends unemployment

indicators.note: organised means arranged into a new order, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A planned island brings joblessness to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without work, being unoccupied, is the state of having nothing to do.

clue.text: Ceremony with religious song lacking special mysticism at heart

indicators.note: lacking says the following letters go missing from the song

parts.note: a spiritual is a religious folk song from the American South

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter

explanation.surface: A rite with a hymn that lacks any special core of mysticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' gives I, the middle letter of 'mysticism'; SP and I come off the front of SPIRITUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal religious or solemn rite performed in a set way is a ceremonial observance.

clue.text: Element of regret over narcotic

indicators.note: over says the regret word is turned backwards

parts.note: to rue is to regret
opium is a narcotic drug from poppies

explanation.surface: Part of someone's remorse about a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Element' suggests a part of the regret, but it is a chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: This rare-earth metal, number 63, is a chemical element named after Europe.

clue.text: Impressive English politician has curtailed time in charge

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, so the word loses its tail letter

explanation.surface: An English MP cuts short a stint in office.
explanation.definitionFit: Forceful and striking, with strong emphasis, is how an emphatic statement comes across.

clue.text: Out of consideration employees finally quit living accommodation

parts.note: apart, as in joking apart, means set aside and not considered
men are workers or employees

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Staff no longer considered finally leave their housing.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat, a set of rooms to live in, is a type of dwelling.

clue.text: Unruffled involving publicity for lover's song, maybe

indicators.note: involving means enclosing, so the publicity letters sit inside

parts.note: serene means calm and unruffled
an ad is an advertisement, publicity

explanation.surface: A calm promotion for a romantic ballad.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor's night music beneath a window is the classic example; 'maybe' marks this as one kind.

clue.text: Eccentric Nineties physicist

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre or odd, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A quirky scientist of the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert of relativity fame is the most famous of all physicists.

clue.text: Lack of movement as one European boards broken-down train

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: boards means gets on, so the European letter goes inside
broken-down means wrecked, so the letters of train are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller from Europe boards a train that has broken down and goes nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken-down' turns TRAIN into NRTIA, and 'boards' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stillness or sluggishness, a resistance to change of motion, is the physics sense.

clue.text: Fit in cubicle

parts.note: a stall is a compartment or cubicle, as in a shower stall

explanation.surface: Something that would fit inside a booth.
explanation.definitionFit: To fit a kitchen or appliance is to set it up in place.

clue.text: Cherish sinner, he changed

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Love the sinner, he has reformed.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold something sacred, to preserve it reverently, is to treasure it.

clue.text: Record section of confusing lecture

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A recording of part of a baffling talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-track release on vinyl or download is a type of record.

clue.text: Part-time worker recalled the Spanish religious building

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the article is reversed

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A temporary worker called back to a Spanish church.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrine or place of worship, such as a Hindu or Greek one, is this kind of building.

clue.text: Ornament with little loops in centre of hand-picked baby bed

indicators.note: the centre of the ten-letter word is its middle two letters

parts.note: a cot is a baby's bed

explanation.surface: A decoration with little loops in the middle of a carefully chosen crib.
explanation.definitionFit: A small embroidered loop forming a decorative edging on lace or ribbon is this trim.

clue.text: Manufacturer adding barrels to stocks

parts.note: a firearm is made of a barrel fixed to a wooden stock, so the maker fits one to the other, not adding to inventory

explanation.surface: A firm adding barrels to its supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barrels' and 'stocks' suggest casks and inventory; they are parts of a rifle.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who makes and repairs firearms is this tradesman.

clue.text: Dreadful toccatas with each note disconnected

indicators.note: dreadful means terrible, so the letters are put into a mess

explanation.surface: Awful toccatas played with every note detached.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction for short, detached notes played separately is this Italian term.

clue.text: Unaccompanied student merely goes round Spain

parts.note: L is a learner, a student driver

indicators.note: goes round means encircles, so the merely word wraps around the Spain letter

parts.note: only means merely
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A solitary student merely tours Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alone, without companions, is the sense of solitary here.

clue.text: Abuse whisky on a trip, initially

parts.note: a malt is a malt whisky
re means about or on, as in regarding

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Whisky abuse on a trip, at first.
explanation.definitionFit: To mistreat or handle cruelly is to abuse someone.
